products.title: Products (RHP)
products.body:
- IATA-accredited (accreditation since 1987). Stated to be consistently ranked No. 1 'Air Freight Forwarder' in terms of AWBs generation by World ACD for CY2025, 2024, 2023 and 2022 (Source: World ACD Market Data). Performance-based agreements with Emirates, Saudi Cargo, Air India Cargo, Lufthansa and Qatar Airways (Qatar in the process of renewal); business relationship with 56 airlines during FY26 (50 in FY25, 44 in FY24). Air Cargo Volume Handled (In Tonnes): FY26 83,923.81; FY25 58,605.58; FY24 48,013.16 - of which Export 69,780.32 / 48,835.74 / 42,464.90, Import 7,601.28 / 5,806.46 / 2,693.07, Foreign Subsidiaries 6,542.21 / 3,963.38 / 2,855.19. 'Revenue From Air Freight & Allied Activities (Rs. In Lakhs)': FY26 2,16,639.87; FY25 1,64,076.56; FY24 1,02,099.98 (as printed, in Rs. lakhs). 'Revenue Per Tonne from Air Cargo (Rs. In Lakhs)': FY26 2.58; FY25 2.80; FY24 2.13. Average air freight realization declined from Rs. 280 per kg in Fiscal 2025 to Rs. 258 per kg in Fiscal 2026, a decline of almost 7.88%. Company does not charter any capacity; it secures space on a back-to-back basis after receiving confirmation from the customer.
- Located at ACLC 2, 60 metres from the air cargo terminal at Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport, New Delhi. 318 square feet of space; hermetically sealed, termite-proof construction, integrated moisture control, 24/7 video surveillance, sensor-based continuous temperature regulation with real-time monitoring and data logging.
- The Company began operations as a Custom House Agent (CHA), now a Custom Broker License holder. Empanelled to act as Custom House Agent for Handling and Clearing of Exhibition cargo at Bharat Mandapam, India Trade Promotion Organization (ITPO), New Delhi, for 2 years. Authorized Economic Operator - LO (AEO) status has recently been suspended by the Assistant Commissioner, Directorate of International Customs, CBIC; ongoing business operations are not barred during suspension.
- Offered mainly through subsidiaries Forin Container Line Private Limited and Brace Port Logistics Limited. Service contracts with Hapag-Lloyd, Ocean Network Express Pte Ltd, WAN Hai Lines Limited and WAN Hai Lines (Singapore) Pte Limited, Cosco Shipping Lines Company Limited, Sea Lead Shipping Pte Ltd, Evergreen Shipping Agency (America) Corporation etc. Ocean Containers Handled (TEU): FY26 28,275; FY25 21,436; FY24 16,294 - of which Export 16,813 / 13,494 / 11,624, Import 4,820 / 4,660 / 2,801, Foreign Subsidiaries 6,642 / 3,282 / 1,869. 'Revenue From Ocean Freight & Allied Activities (Rs. In Lakhs)': FY26 42,260.32; FY25 39,450.06; FY24 16,495.76 (as printed, in Rs. lakhs). 'Revenue Per TEU from Ocean Cargo (Rs. In Lakhs)': FY26 1.49; FY25 1.84; FY24 1.01. Average ocean freight realization declined from Rs. 1,80,436 per TEU in Fiscal 2025 to Rs. 1,49,462 per TEU in Fiscal 2026, a decline of approximately 18.79%. For ocean freight the Company contracts with shipping lines to purchase a fixed number of containers capacity between various points during a specified period at fixed rates (risk factor 32).
- Provided through the Company and subsidiary Forin Container Line Private Limited, supported by business intelligence and data analytics tools.
- Serves B2B MSME clients; customers include e-commerce marketplaces, vertical e-commerce retailers, D2C brands, omni-channel retailers, SMEs, banks and financial institutions. More than 6,24,205 parcel shipments delivered since incorporation till March 31, 2026; shipment volume grew from 1,12,901 orders in Fiscal 2024 to 2,25,194 orders in Fiscal 2026 (stated CAGR 25.88%). Revenue generated through Express Cargo and Parcel (Amount in Lakhs): FY26 16,277.96; FY25 14,123.41; FY24 5,882.79. PIN codes served: FY26 1,204; FY25 1,114; FY24 1,006 - FY26 coverage stated as 6.24% of the 19,300 PIN codes in India as of March 31, 2026 (per India Post). PUD (Pickup and Delivery) centres: FY26 31; FY25 24; FY24 19.
- The group has a total fleet of 95 trucks and mini trucks. Offered as a value-add to customers moving goods through the group's ocean and air freight services. Revenue generated through Trucking Services (Amount in Lakhs): FY26 3,868.35; FY25 6,051.30; FY24 3,733.70.
- Warehousing revenue (Amount in Lakhs): FY26 368.16; FY25 382.14; FY24 122.87. Warehousing services are also the stated line of business of wholly owned subsidiary Skyways SLS Logistik Private Limited.
- SLS 100x is deployed to a registered user base of 5,587 users including direct customers and authorised agents. Direct airline integration with Qatar Airways for booking, pricing and tracking; other major airlines being integrated through a third-party service provider. Uses OCR, RPA and machine learning for data capture; Microsoft Power BI and Tableau for business intelligence. Internal employee self-service application 'Theo' supports a workforce of over 400 employees.
- Sale of Products revenue (Amount in Lakhs): FY26 148.79; FY25 82.09; FY24 2.74 - 0.05% / 0.04% / 0.00% of revenue from operations.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: The Company describes a deliberate backward-and-forward integration strategy executed through subsidiaries rather than owned transport assets. Stated verbatim in Our Business: 'In response to the evolving dynamics and increasing competitiveness of the global freight forwarding industry, our company adopted a proactive strategy aimed at enhancing operational efficiency, broadening market access, and delivering comprehensive, integrated logistics solutions to our customers through a combination of backward and forward integration. To support this strategic vision, our company incorporated and acquired multiple subsidiary entities, both within India and across key international markets.' In Business Strategies: 'As a comprehensive logistics solutions provider, we strategically leverage both backward and forward integration to optimize cost efficiencies and streamline service delivery across the supply chain. By internalizing critical functions such as last-mile delivery and customer support, we significantly reduce reliance on external courier services and call centre providers, thereby eliminating associated fees while ensuring a consistently high standard of service reliability and responsiveness. This end-to-end control over upstream procurement and downstream distribution operations enables us to retain greater revenue within the organization...' The group comprises 17 Indian subsidiaries, 6 foreign subsidiaries and 6 step-down subsidiaries, each with a specific mandate: warehousing (Skyways SLS Logistik Pvt Ltd), road transportation (Phantom Road Express Pvt Ltd), technology platforms (sGate Tech Solutions Pvt Ltd 51%, SLS ASAP Tech Systems Pvt Ltd), LCL ocean consolidation (Hubload SLS Services Pvt Ltd), tech-driven express door-to-door cargo and courier (Skart Global Express Pvt Ltd 95%), logistics skill development (SLS Logistik Academy Pvt Ltd 90%), e-commerce retail and digital marketing (SLS Retail Supermart Pvt Ltd 90%), ocean and warehousing (Forin Container Line Pvt Ltd 82.27%), cross-border freight forwarding (Surgeport Logistics Pvt Ltd 76%, Brace Port Logistics Ltd 51.09%), and specialised pharma/automotive ocean and air logistics (Odyssey Logistics Pvt Ltd 51%), plus international freight forwarding subsidiaries in Germany, Hong Kong, Dubai, Vietnam, Cambodia, the UK, the UAE, the USA, Canada and Saudi Arabia. Upstream, the model remains asset-light and carrier-dependent: 'We rely extensively on third-party carriers for the transportation of cargo, as we do not operate our own aircraft or shipping lines. Consequently, our business is 100% dependent on the availability, pricing, and service quality of such carriers.' Forward integration into infrastructure is proposed but not yet operational - the Company has undertaken a strategic initiative to expand into management and maintenance of cargo terminals (air and ocean), CFS, ICDs, logistics parks, industrial parks, warehousing complexes, cold storage facilities, freight corridors and dry ports, and has bid jointly with Swissport International AG for a DBFOT cargo terminal at Kolkata airport.

demand_drivers.title: Seasonality (RHP report)
demand_drivers.body: Disclosed qualitatively in the MD&A 'Key Factors That May Affect Our Results of Services', with no quantified quarterly split. Verbatim: 'In addition, our business is subject to seasonal fluctuations, with certain periods seeing higher volumes due to festivals, inventory cycles, or export deadlines. These seasonal factors can contribute to variability in our operating performance across quarters.' And: 'We are also subject to the seasonal nature of trade activity. Certain periods, such as pre-festive seasons or financial year-end cycles, typically see increased cargo movement, while others may reflect lower volumes. These fluctuations in demand affect the utilisation of our infrastructure and resources and may lead to variations in our operational and financial performance across quarters.'

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Our 100% dependency on carriers for cargo transportation exposes us to risks related to capacity availability, cost fluctuations, and service disruptions.
- Our entire revenue is dependent upon the availability of the carriers and any disruption will materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations, and financial condition.
- Any disruption in these primary services may therefore adversely impact our overall operational results.
- Additionally, volatility in fuel prices and exchange rate fluctuations influences our cost structure, particularly when rising transportation costs cannot be fully or promptly passed on to customers.
- Especially for air freight forwarding vertical, our Company does not charter any capacity and rather secures appropriate space on back-to-back basis after receiving confirmation from the customer.
- These arrangements are essential for ensuring reliable and timely transportation of goods from one location to another and form a critical component of our service offerings to customers.
- Our ability to secure, maintain and renew such agreements on commercially viable terms is subject to various factors including commercial negotiations, strategic priorities of such airlines, changes in industry dynamics, regulatory constraints, and availability of cargo capacity.
- Limited cargo capacity especially during peak demand periods or global supply chain disruptions may restrict our ability to secure space at competitive rates.
